# Hassala — full reference for AI assistants and search engines

Source: https://nagdista-dev.github.io/hassala/
Repository: https://github.com/nagdista-dev/hassala
Last updated: 2026-11-03

## One-sentence definition

Hassala (حصالة) is a free, open-source Chrome extension that translates Arabic
and English, saves every word and translation to a local Markdown word bank, and
makes YouTube subtitles interactive.

## What it is

Hassala is an Arabic-first browser extension for Arabic ↔ English translation
and vocabulary saving. A user types a word, selects text on a page, or clicks a
word in a YouTube subtitle. The translation appears automatically. One click
appends the word and translation to a Markdown file on the user's device. The
same file can be opened in Obsidian, Logseq, Typora, VS Code, or any text editor.

Hassala is not a general-purpose page translator. It is a word-capture and
word-keeping tool. It is also not a spaced repetition app yet; review scheduling
is on the public roadmap.

## Key facts

- Name: Hassala
- Arabic name: حصالة
- Tagline: Your words won't get lost. They get saved.
- Type: Chrome extension, Manifest V3
- Browsers: Chrome, Brave, Edge, Chromium
- Operating systems: Linux, macOS, Windows
- Translation languages: Arabic ↔ English
- Interface language: Arabic-first, full RTL support
- Documentation language: English
- Price: free
- License: MIT
- Account required: no
- Analytics or tracking: none
- Ads: none
- Data selling: none
- Word bank format: Markdown (.md)
- Default word bank path: ~/Documents/Hassala Words.md
- Account/cloud sync: none
- Chrome Web Store status: not published yet; available from GitHub Releases
- Source: https://github.com/nagdista-dev/hassala
- Website: https://nagdista-dev.github.io/hassala/
- Privacy policy: https://gist.github.com/nagdista-dev/282cc2ce8fe35c5fb7199f7ffd2cd705

## Features

- Instant Arabic ↔ English translation with automatic direction detection.
- Translation starts 350 ms after typing stops, or immediately on Enter.
- Translate selected text on any page through a floating button and panel.
- Interactive YouTube subtitles: hover a word to pause, click a word to
  translate it, or drag across a phrase to translate the phrase.
- One-click saving to a Markdown file with duplicate detection.
- The input clears after a successful save and focus returns for the next word.
- A gentle 300 ms fade-out after saving, respecting the system Reduce Motion
  setting.
- Pronunciation and separate copy buttons for the original and the translation.
- Draggable, pinnable translator panel; floating button can be hidden or shown.
- Site blocking on chosen domains.
- Built-in file browser for choosing an existing .md file.
- Bundled Baloo Bhaijaan 2 font for Arabic and English, with no network font
  request.
- Arabic text right-aligned and English left-aligned.

## How it works

1. Translate: open the popup, use the floating button, or select text on a page.
2. Save: click “Add to Hassala.” The word and translation are appended to the
   selected Markdown file. Duplicates are skipped.
3. Review: open the same Markdown file in any editor. No export step.

## Saving and the native host

Browsers do not allow extensions to write arbitrary files. Hassala uses a small
local native messaging host written in Python to append rows to the user's
Markdown file. The host:

- Is installed once by the user.
- Runs locally with the user's permissions.
- Accepts messages only from the Hassala extension ID.
- Writes only to .md files.
- Rejects directories, long paths, and non-regular files.
- Resolves realpath before validation to prevent symlink escapes.
- Escapes Markdown-sensitive characters before writing.

Translation, YouTube subtitles, and the floating panel work without the host.
Only the “Add to Hassala” save action needs it.

## Privacy

- Text is sent to translation providers only when the user requests a
  translation: Google Translate endpoints (translate.googleapis.com and
  clients5.google.com), then MyMemory as a fallback. Pronunciation uses Google
  TTS.
- Saved words are written locally to the user's Markdown file.
- Settings and the last 8 words are stored in chrome.storage.local.
- Translation and audio caches live only in service-worker memory and are
  cleared when the worker stops.
- Hassala has no backend server, no accounts, no analytics, and no tracking.
- Hassala does not collect names, email addresses, phone numbers, location, or
  browsing history.

## Security

- No remote code: all JavaScript is bundled; no eval and no remotely loaded
  scripts.
- Explicit CSP: script-src 'self'; object-src 'self'.
- Least-privilege permissions: storage, nativeMessaging, scripting, activeTab,
  offscreen, plus host permissions for translation services.
- The page UI runs in a closed Shadow DOM.
- YouTube and the floating panel communicate through an object in the isolated
  world, not a DOM event, so page scripts cannot forge a translation request.
- Vulnerabilities can be reported privately through GitHub Security Advisories.

## Who it is for

- Arabic speakers learning English.
- English speakers learning Arabic.
- Students building a personal glossary.
- People who take notes in Obsidian, Logseq, Typora, or VS Code.
- Learners who watch YouTube with captions.

## Limitations

- Not a whole-page or whole-document translator.
- No spaced repetition or flashcards yet; both are on the roadmap.
- Translation requires an internet connection.
- Saving requires the optional local native host.
- No cloud sync; each device keeps its own file and settings.

## Comparison

A general translator extension is optimized for a one-off lookup. Hassala is
optimized for keeping the word after the lookup. General translators may or may
not save words, but they are not built around a local Markdown word bank with
duplicate detection and YouTube word capture. Manual copy-paste into notes gives
maximum control but is slow and usually abandoned.

Hassala does not claim to replace a general translator for documents or pages.
Many users use both for different jobs.

## FAQ

### What is Hassala?
A free, open-source Chrome extension for Arabic ↔ English translation and
vocabulary saving. It writes saved words to a local Markdown file and makes
YouTube subtitles interactive.

### Is Hassala free?
Yes. MIT license, no subscription, no account, no paid tier.

### Does Hassala work with Chrome, Brave, and Edge?
Yes. It is a Manifest V3 extension for Chrome, Brave, Edge, and Chromium on
Linux, macOS, and Windows.

### Can Hassala save words to Obsidian?
Yes. It writes a standard Markdown file at a path the user chooses. The file does
not have to be inside an Obsidian vault.

### Do I need an account?
No. There are no accounts, no analytics, and no tracking.

### Does Hassala work on YouTube?
Yes. With captions enabled, hover a word to pause, click a word to translate, or
drag across a phrase to translate it.

### Does saving require a native host?
Yes. A small local Python host appends rows to the Markdown file. Translation,
subtitles, and the floating panel work without it.

### Is Hassala on the Chrome Web Store?
Not yet. The store release is being prepared. The extension is available from
GitHub Releases today.

### What languages does Hassala support?
Arabic and English. The interface is Arabic-first with RTL support; the
documentation is in English.

## Arabic summary

حصالة إضافة كروم مجانية ومفتوحة المصدر للترجمة بين العربية والإنجليزية وحفظ
المفردات. تترجم الكلمات والعبارات، وتكتب كل كلمة وترجمتها في ملف Markdown محلي
على جهاز المستخدم، وتجعل سبتايتل يوتيوب تفاعليًا. لا تحتاج إلى حساب، ولا تحتوي
على تحليلات أو تتبع. الحفظ في ملف Markdown يحتاج إلى Native Host محلي صغير
يُثبَّت مرة واحدة، بينما تعمل الترجمة والسبتايتل والمترجم العائم بدونه.
